marble.name: Parts of a Plant
marble.subject: Science
marble.description: Identify and describe the basic structure of common flowering plants (roots, stem, leaves, flowers) and trees (roots, trunk, branches, leaves)
marble.prompt: If you pick a flower from the garden, can you point to the roots, stem, leaves, and petals and say what each part does?

cluster.summary: Your child is learning about the amazing diversity of life — identifying different animals and plants, understanding how body parts help animals survive, and discovering what all living things need to stay alive.

misconceptions: Omitting or forgetting the roots because they are hidden underground — 'the plant starts at the soil'.
Not recognising a tree as a plant with the same basic parts (trunk = woody stem).
Thinking the stem is just a 'stick' with no role, or that leaves are only for looks.
Confusing flower and fruit, or believing all plants have showy flowers.
representations: A labelled whole-plant diagram (roots, stem, leaves, flower) with the roots shown in a soil cross-section.
Flowering-plant and tree side by side with equivalent parts linked (stem–trunk).
A real pulled-up plant / potted plant for first-hand observation.
Drag-the-label or build-a-plant part cards (roots, stem, leaf, flower).
authoredAnswer: Correctly points to and names roots, stem, leaves, flower (and tree: roots, trunk, branches, leaves). Says the roots take in WATER (and hold the plant steady in the ground). Full marks pair correct labelling with roots doing water uptake, not just 'holding on'.

wrongAnswers.wrong: The roots are just there to hold the plant in the soil.
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: names roots but gives only anchoring, not water uptake
wrongAnswers.fix: Stand celery in coloured water — the colour climbs, showing roots/stem take water IN, not just hold on. Anchoring is one job of two.

wrongAnswers.wrong: A tree isn't a plant, so it doesn't have the same parts.
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: treats tree and plant as separate categories; won't map trunk↔stem
wrongAnswers.fix: Line up a small plant and a tree — both have roots, a stem (the trunk is a woody stem), leaves. A tree is a big plant.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: labels leaves but has no functional sense of them
wrongAnswers.fix: Preview that leaves catch sunlight (their job comes next) — for now, fix that every part is there for a reason.
